messages.text: Based on current vault evidence, what are the strongest opportunities for Signaling / Non-signaling Tester in AI, and what evidence supports each opportunity?

The knowledge base gave **no validated answer** for a complete “strongest opportunities” comparison, mainly because the evidence did not validate a direct AI-market relationship for every item. However, it did return usable Raw evidence for several tester opportunities. Based only on that vault evidence, the strongest supported opportunities are:

| Rank | Opportunity for Signaling / Non-signaling Tester | Why it looks strong | Vault evidence |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **AI-assisted CMX500 test automation / scripting** | This is the only opportunity directly tied to AI in the returned Raw evidence. It points to the **CMX500 AI Scripting Assistant**, positioned as AI-driven automation for mobile device testing and shown at MWC 2025. | Raw evidence says the “CMX500 AI Scripting Assistant” is available through deployment options and was demonstrated live at MWC 2025 Barcelona. Source: `raw/Productions/PR/CMX500 AI Scripting Assistant from Rohde & Schwarz facilitates mobile device testing through AI-driven automation.md` [65] |
| 2 | **CMX500 as a unified wireless R&D signaling platform for AI-enabled devices** | AI devices increasingly need multiple radios and standards. The evidence supports CMX500 as a **multi-technology, multi-channel signaling tester** covering cellular and non-cellular testing in one setup, including Wi‑Fi 7. The AI-device angle is an inference; the multi-standard tester capability is supported. | Raw evidence states CMX500 is a multi-technology, multi-channel signaling tester with newly added Wi‑Fi 7 testing capabilities for LTE/5G/WLAN-type operation testing in a single instrument setup. Source: `raw/Productions/PR/Rohde & Schwarz presents its Wi-Fi 7 multi-channel single-box test solutions for R&D and production at MWC 2024.md` [68] |
| 3 | **Power-consumption / energy-efficiency testing for connected AI devices** | AI-enabled mobile, IoT and edge devices are power-sensitive. The evidence supports CMX500 being used with SmartViser for power-consumption measurements alongside RF, protocol or application tests. The “AI device” relevance is an inference; the energy-efficiency test capability is supported. | Raw evidence says the SmartViser/R&S solution combines with CMX500 and enables seamless power consumption measurements alongside RF, protocol or application tests. Source: `raw/Productions/PR/Rohde & Schwarz and SmartViser partner to demonstrate test solutions for new EEI regulation.md` [67] |
| 4 | **NTN / satellite-connected AI and IoT device testing with CMX500** | Edge AI and IoT may use non-terrestrial connectivity in remote deployments. The returned evidence only supports CMX500 as having an NTN testing entry point, not a direct AI use case. | Raw evidence points to more information on “the CMX500 for NTN testing.” Source: `raw/Productions/PR/Rohde & Schwarz and Viasat to collaborate on NB-NTN IoT test plan for connectivity via satellite.md` [66] |
| 5 | **CMP180 high-bandwidth waveform testing for future wireless R&D/production** | For non-signaling or waveform-oriented test needs, CMP180 has evidence around 480 MHz bandwidth waveform verification in loopback mode for R&D and production. The vault result notes that the Raw passage does **not** explicitly label CMP180 as “non-signaling,” and it is not directly tied to AI. | Raw evidence says CMP180 will verify a 480 MHz bandwidth signal waveform in loopback mode for users in R&D and production. Source: `raw/Productions/PR/Rohde & Schwarz presents its Wi-Fi 7 multi-channel single-box test solutions for R&D and production at MWC 2024.md` [68] |

**Bottom line from the vault evidence:**  
The strongest directly supported AI opportunity is **CMX500 AI-assisted scripting / automation**. The other opportunities—multi-radio AI devices, energy-efficiency testing, NTN-connected AI/IoT, and high-bandwidth waveform testing—are plausible AI-adjacent opportunities, but the returned Raw evidence supports the tester capabilities rather than a direct AI-market linkage.

data.answer:
已查到可引用的部分資料：

### Supported opportunities from RAW
| Product line | Opportunity supported by RAW | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| CMX500 | AI-assisted CMX500 scripting/tooling is the clearest AI-linked opportunity, because the “CMX500 AI Scripting Assistant” is available through deployment options and was shown live at MWC 2025 Barcelona. | [65] |
| CMX500 | CMX500 can support wireless device R&D across cellular and non-cellular standards in one setup, because RAW states it is a multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester with newly added Wi‑Fi 7 testing capabilities for LTE/5G/WLAN-type operation testing in a single instrument setup. | [68] |
| CMX500 | CMX500 can support energy-efficiency and power-consumption testing in parallel with RF, protocol, or application tests, because RAW states the SmartViser/R&S solution combines with CMX500 and offers seamless power consumption measurements alongside those tests. | [67] |
| CMX500 | CMX500 has an NTN testing entry point, because RAW points to more information on “the CMX500 for NTN testing.” | [66] |
| CMP180 | CMP180 has a future-proof R&D/production waveform-test opportunity beyond Wi‑Fi 7, because RAW states it will verify a 480 MHz bandwidth signal waveform in loopback mode for users in R&D and production. | [68] |
### Not supported by RAW
| Requested area | RAW support status |
|---|---|
| CMP180 as “non-signaling” | RAW passage [68] supports CMP180 waveform loopback for R&D and production, but does not state “non-signaling.” |
【推論】The only directly AI-named tester opportunity in RAW is CMX500 AI Scripting Assistant, while CMX500 Wi‑Fi 7, CMX500 energy-efficiency testing, CMX500 NTN testing, and CMP180 480 MHz waveform loopback are adjacent tester opportunities not directly tied to AI by RAW. [65][66][67][68]
